claims.text: MaxReach is a 30-agent content production platform in which each agent has exactly one defined role and no agent does two jobs.

MaxReach's pipeline has eight sequential stages with two fan-out points: input, research, strategy fan-out, persuasion brief, writer draft, quality gate, human approval gate, and adapter fan-out to six destinations.

In MaxReach's strategy stage, three analysts run in parallel (competitive content landscape, ICP profile, expertise signals), then a strategy reviewer validates their outputs and a strategy aggregator merges them into a single plan referenced by all downstream steps.

MaxReach's quality gate has four sequential checks (fact-checker against research output, AI detector, neuro-optimizer checking the persuasion brief is reflected, and a review agent for consistency and brand voice); all four must pass or the content does not advance.

MaxReach's human approval gate sits between the quality gate and the adapters; a Telegram bot gives the editor one-tap approve or reject, and nothing publishes without an explicit approve signal, so the human reviews one version instead of six.
MaxReach publishes to six channels (WordPress, DevTo, Hashnode, LinkedIn, Telegram Channel, Astro) via six adapter agents and publisher agents that push in parallel.

MaxReach uses 918 automated tests validating pipeline transitions, agent output schemas, queue behavior and publishing integrations; a job does not advance unless the upstream output matches the expected schema.

MaxReach is multi-tenant: each brand has its own ICP, voice specification, competitor data and channel configuration, which agents resolve at runtime, so the same writer agent produces different brand content without code changes.

MaxReach's reported results: 15+ hours per week of production coordination replaced, six channels managed simultaneously (previously 1 to 2), and two people now run a six-channel publishing operation; the case study gives no throughput or performance metrics beyond this.
MaxReach has an analytics feedback loop in which three analytics agents and a hypothesis-generator feed performance insights back into the strategy stage.

Opuslon built a three-agent sequential system for the marketing agency Wasel.ma, where each agent receives the previous agent's output and has access only to the data its role needs (CRM, analytics, client drive).

In the Wasel.ma system, a strategist agent runs every Monday, synthesizing the brand brief, live data (Search Console, last week's results, competitor moves) and market trends into a weekly brief that a human approves on Telegram before execution.

In the Wasel.ma system, agents do not call each other; they read and write Markdown files (BRAND_BRIEF.md, CAMPAIGN_BRIEF.md, RESULTS.md, SEO_REPORT.md, CRM.md) in a shared Obsidian vault, which serves as the audit trail and limits what a compromised agent can see.
The Wasel.ma system uses an expensive model only for the weekly strategist and the lead-qualifying mailer, and a cheap model for content, publisher and FAQ-reply agents, to control cost.

In the Wasel.ma system, final publishing and email sending require human validation via Telegram, and a mailer agent auto-replies to FAQ/pricing questions while escalating hot leads and demo requests to a human.
Reported Wasel.ma results: content volume x4 without hiring and commercial response time reduced from 24 hours to 2 hours.

Google Cloud Marketing agentified its integrated campaign workflow: an agent scans calendars and budgets, generates three brief options for a human to review and approve, distributes the approved strategy, localizes, translates and resizes assets under human supervision, runs brand compliance checks, and marketing leadership gives final sign-off.
Google Cloud Marketing reports its agentified campaign workflow is 2X to 3X faster, compressing a weeklong cycle into two days.

Google Cloud Marketing uses a manager review rubric for AI agents with four criteria: accuracy, speed, brand compliance and value; it also formed temporary 'AI pods' of three to five people paired with a workflow architect.

Draft & Goal is a commercial 'Agentic Marketing OS' platform where routes coordinate specialized agents, multiple models, company knowledge and integrations, with people approving at every step that matters.
Draft & Goal claims production results of TotalEnergies going from 2 to 24 articles a day and Turo shipping tens of thousands of pages at about $1 each (vendor claims).

Draft & Goal's Google Ads agents query search_term_view via GAQL, flag terms that spend without converting, and draft negative keywords held for human review, with no account changes without sign-off.

MERIDIAN (Gruntflow) is a planner-led multi-agent content engine with one planner and six specialists, posting to Meta, X and LinkedIn; a critic agent checks brand voice and tone, logs every rejection, and a human keeps the final veto.
MERIDIAN feeds performance analytics back into the brief rather than the model, so the learning is human-readable and overridable.

SaaStr runs its AI operation with 3 humans and 21+ AI agents; for one event its sales agents booked 614 meetings at roughly $85K average ticket size, with about 2.25 million site sessions and about 402,000 interactions handled.
